issues.legal_issue: Land that has already vested in the State upon possession under an acquisition cannot be revested by a later effective vesting under a separate estates statute, and the earlier vesting does not justify denying compensation in the acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: Possession of the land was taken under the acquisition proceedings before the effective date on which a notification under the estates statute declared the land would vest in the State.
The land vested in the State free from encumbrances when possession was taken under the acquisition proceedings.
The High Court held that the landowners were not entitled to compensation, and the matter came before the Supreme Court in appeals concerning the State’s appeal and the landowners’ cross-objection.
issues.conclusion: The land, having already vested in the State upon possession, could not be revested by the later effective vesting under the estates statute. The High Court was wrong to deny compensation on that basis; its judgment was set aside and the State’s appeal and the landowners’ cross-objection were remanded to the High Court for decision in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, possession could be taken without waiting for the award, and the land vested in the State free from encumbrances upon that possession. A later vesting under Section 4 of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act could not revest land that had already vested. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether compensation is payable for land acquired by the State.
predicates.possession_preceded_later_effective_vest: Possession of the land was taken before a separate statutory vesting of that land became effective.
predicates.land_vested_on_possession: Taking possession caused the land to vest in the State free from encumbrances.
predicates.prior_vesting_precludes_revesting_and_co: Land already vested in the State cannot be revested by the later statutory vesting, and that later vesting cannot be used to deny compensation in the acquisition proceedings.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal concerns land that vested in the State upon possession before a separate statutory vesting became effective, the earlier vesting prevents revesting and cannot support denial of compensation.
